HON. RAMIR A. BARRAMEDA Vice-Mayor Municipality of Basud Province of Camarines Norte Dear Vice-Mayor Barrameda: s. 202. This has reference to the letter dated 21 January 2019 of former Vice-Mayor Silverio G. Quiäones III, requesting for the Department's enlightenment on the following queries, which we quoted hereunder in toto: ii. Ifthe DILG-13 Opinion No. 17 dated May 8, 2012 issued by the Regional Director of CARAGA Region is not yet superseded and still in effect, and could be used as basis in Executive Order No. 002-2019 dated January 8, 2019 issued by our Municipal Mayor. If all MOOE under regular PPAs included in the Annual Investment Program duly adopted by the Municipal Development Council (MDC) for FY 2019 could be included in the reenacted budget particularly in the offices that provides frontline services, such as: Municipal Health Office, Municipal Agriculture Office, Municipal Social Welfare Office, and MDRRMO. If not what are the specific expenses that are covered by a reenacted budget under the said offices. If the Job Order Employees with expire contract whose functions are technical and not covered by the functions of any of the regular employees within the office can be renewed under a reenacted budget. Per letter of Mr. Quiriones III, Municipal Mayor Adrian S. Davoco issued Executive Order No. 002-2019, entitled "AN ORDER AUTHORIZING THE DISBURSEMENT OF 2018 MAINTENANCE AND OTHER OPERATING EXPENSES (MOOE) AND THE SALARIES AND WAGES OF ALL EXISTING POSITIONS INCLUDING STATUTORY AND CONTRACTUAL OBLIGATIONS OF THE LGU UNDER REENACTED BUDGET PURSUANT TO SECTION 323 OF THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 "on January 8, 2019, for failure of the Sangguniang Bayan of Basud to enact the annual appropriations for 2019. He also stated that the Sangguniang Bayan is in favor with the implementation of a reenacted budget while your budget for 2019 is yet to be approved. Contrary to the Executive Order issued by the Mayor, the Sanggunian is of the belief that not all object of expenditures of the Annual Budget of the

preceding year shall be covered by the Executive Order, as there are only selected items from the MOOE identified as essential to operations are qualified for disbursements pursuant to Section 323 of the Local Government Code, to wit: "In case the Sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuring fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during sessions. If the Sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concerned. However, annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. " xxx Hence, the above-quoted queries. Foremost, it is imperative to distinguish MOOE from essential operating expenses. MOOE is defined under the Glossary of Terms, Operations Manual for Local Government Units 2016 Edition, as an allocation to support the operations of local government units including those for supplies and materials, transportation and travel, utilities and other maintenance activities. On the other hand, essential operating expenses pursuant to Second Paragraph, Item 1.5 of the Budget Operations Manual for Local Government Units 2016 Edition refers to specific objects of expenditure under maintenance and other operating expenses, which are necessary for the operation of a particular local government unit to carry out its mandate in providing efficient and effective basic services. The local government unit is in best position to identify expenses which, according to its best judgment, are essential to its operation. On the first and second queries, although the local chief executive primarily determines what are the essential operating expenses, consistent with the definition given above, the Department in its Legal Opinion No. 42,s.2018 has opined that only "essential" (of the utmost importance; indispensable; extremely necessaryl) and not all operating expenses should be included in the MOOE. Thus, DILG-13 Opinion No. 17 dated May 8, 2012 issued by the Regional Director of CARAGA Region is already superseded and could no longer be the basis of Executive Order No. 002-2019. 1 https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/essential

With respect to the third query, this Department is of the view that Job Order Employees can be renewed in a reenacted budget. Job Orders covers piece of work or intermittent job of short duration not exceeding six months on a daily basis and are not considered government service but are in the nature of contracts which is under the supervision and regulation by the DBM and COA pursuant to Section 1, Rule XI of Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular No. 40,S.1998, as amended, and CSC MC No. 01, S.2007. Hence, renewal thereof may be covered under the reenacted budget provided said contractual obligation was authorized in the annual and supplemental budget for the preceding year2. Since you are now the incumbent Vice-Mayor of Basud, Camarines Norte, we deemed it appropriate to address this concern to you, and for you to inform Mr. Quifiones III of this legal opinion. We hope to have addressed the concern sufficiently. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secr tary: MARIVEL C. ACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary CC: Atty. Anthony C.
